summary.headline: You have enough resolved cases to seed a cold-start eval set — now assign a named owner and a regression cadence before launch.
summary.narrative: Of 26 cases, 22 are Closed with a usable resolution. We built a 5-case cold-start test set from real in-scope questions (password reset, SSO, teammate invites, exports) with their known-good resolutions. The blocker to launch is observability: no one currently owns AI quality monitoring. Assign that owner, define what to monitor, and set a regression cadence before any AI step.

findings.title: Assign a named owner for AI quality monitoring
findings.what_we_found: No single role currently owns monitoring AI answer quality; monitoring is implied but unassigned.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Unowned monitoring does not happen — regressions and bad answers go unnoticed until a customer complains.
the_fix: Name an accountable owner — recommended: CS Operations Lead (e.g. Dana Reyes) — for AI quality monitoring.
Give them authority to pause AI self-serve on any intent that regresses.
Document the owner and escalation path before go-live.
findings.evidence: No owner assigned in current process.

findings.title: Define what to monitor in production
findings.what_we_found: No agreed monitoring signals exist for a live support AI.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Without defined signals you cannot tell whether the AI is helping or quietly giving wrong answers.
the_fix: Track containment/handoff rate, retrieval-confidence distribution, and escalation reasons.
Track customer sentiment on AI-handled cases.
Flag any answer that contradicts a known-good resolution from the test set for review.

findings.title: Set a regression cadence against the cold-start set
findings.what_we_found: There is no schedule for re-evaluating the AI against the known-good test set.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Prompt, model, or KB changes can silently break previously correct answers if never re-tested.
the_fix: Re-run the cold-start test set weekly and before every prompt or KB change.
Block shipping any change until the set passes.
Grow the set as new in-scope intents gain KB coverage.

drafts.title: Cold-start evaluation set (from resolved cases)
drafts.content:
| # | Case | Question (as asked) | Known-good resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CS-1001 | How do I reset my password? | Use the ‘Forgot password’ link on the sign-in page; a reset email arrives within ~5 minutes. (Self-serve reset link.) |
| 2 | CS-1002 | SSO login fails with a SAML error. | Cause is a misconfigured IdP certificate; walk the admin through correcting the IdP cert configuration. |
| 3 | CS-1005 | How do I invite teammates? | Admins invite members from Settings > Members > Invite (roles: Admin, Member, Viewer). |
| 4 | CS-1022 | Where are my exports stored? | Exports run as background jobs and are retained for 30 days. |
| 5 | CS-1004 | My export isn’t finishing for a large dataset. | Known backend timeout on large datasets; engineering patched it — retry the export. |

Each row pairs a real customer question with its verified resolution. An AI’s answer is graded against the known-good column.
grounded_on: fixtures/customer-success/cases.csv (Closed cases CS-1001, CS-1002, CS-1005, CS-1022, CS-1004)
flags: STARTING SET — human-review each known-good resolution before using it to grade an AI.
Covers in-scope intents only; do not add sensitive intents (billing/security/legal) to this set.
